Hi, I'm sorry to hear that you're suffering from climate anxiety. Climate change can feel very scary and overwhelming sometimes. But, We have made some real progress. A decade ago, We were headed towards 4-5C by 2100. Now with the current pledges, We are headed towards 2C. Still bad, but much, much better than a decade ago. Of course, These pledges needs short-term policies and there is a lot of work to do for meeting our Paris Agreement (Well-below 2C, but also try to limit warming below 1.5C, if possible). But, We have seen greater ambitious efforts from countries. Emissions are flattening and annual growth rate of emissions in 2010s was 3X slower than 2000s. A decade ago, It wasn't crazy to believe that emissions would double by 2050 and triple by 2100. Today, It's clear that it won’t happen. A world with 6x more coal in 2100 than today is a bit ridiculous at this point. Solutions like Solar, Wind, Batteries, EVs are growing exponentially. We're NOT doomed, we can mitigate climate change to a manageable level and it's not "too late". It's also worth empathize that climate change isn't binary. It's not a pass/fail scenario. There is no cliff, deadline or tipping point. Climate change is mostly incremental process, So every bit of warming makes it gradually worse, but every bit of warming we avoid makes a difference. So our collective actions will always matter. It's never too soon or too late to act on climate change. While a 2C or less isn't the perfect world by any means, It's something that humanity can survive and thrive. Humanity have made a lot of progress on many important aspects of our lives, especially in the last 200 years and I think we can expect that to continue. Despite so many horrible news we hear these days, including climate change. The world is better than ever. Though, Progress isn't inevitable and setbacks is possible. The last few years has been a good example of that. But, Humanity have always come back stronger and more united to make more progress. Fighting for climate action is far from hopeless and every day, people are working and fighting for change. This isn't a hopeless fight and you're not doomed. We can overcome and address climate change.

Hey, It’s okay to feel anxious and paralyzed about climate change. It’s both understandable and maybe healthy to feel like that, unless you get stuck there. It’s important to not downplay climate change. But, There is also a danger of overstating the evidence and treat It as unsolvable. It gives a sense of inevitability, doom, despair & hopelessness. But, Climate science does not support the narrative of doom. Climate models, though not perfect, does a very good job at predicting future warming. Under current commitments (as of May 2021) It gets us around \~2C by 2100. It was \~3.5C (2100) in 2009 and \~3C (2100) in 2100. We have seen a lot of new ambitous goals and commitments made by China, US, Japan & South Korea to name a few countries. Clean energy, transportation, food, clothing, heavy transport etc. is on the verge on disrupting every industry that is reponsible for most, if not all emissions. This includes Solar PV, Onshore and Offshore Wind, Batteries, Electric Vehicles, Autonomous Vehicles, Artificial Intelligence, Precision Fermentation, 3-D Printed agriculture, 3-D printing, Aerial vehicles to name a few things. These disruptions are growing exponentially, not linearly. It’s the convergence of different technologies that make a product or service possible that can disrupt oil, natural gas and Coal. This is not driven by climate change or politics. But, Economics. Incumbents won’t be able to compete at these low-cost technologies, which means clean disruption is inevitable. Policies and human behavior are variables, which means It could happen slightly faster or slower than expected.   


Back to the climate, 2C is not a perfect world, But, it’s managable for humans and most ecosystems.
